name: growth-data
note: Growth rings for growth.html, built 2026-10-25. Rings mix measures (sketch, traced or computed built-up land, administrative line); read each ring's 'measure'. WGS84 longitude/latitude.

properties.label: Ōta Dōkan's castle and its small port, 1457 (a sketch, not a survey)
properties.source: Kanto Regional Development Bureau, Tokyo Port Office. (n.d.). 東京港の変遷: 古代・中世 東京港のはじまり [How Tokyo Port changed: ancient and medieval beginnings]. Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism. https://www.pa.ktr.mlit.go.jp/tokyo/history/pdf/e-do01.pdf ; Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Realty. (n.d.). 「日比谷入江」の埋立て [Filling the Hibiya inlet]. このまちアーカイブス. https://smtrc.jp/town-archives/city/hibiya/index.html?id=a01
properties.method: Drawn by hand from written descriptions, not from a map of the time: the castle on the terrace edge, the port near today's Tokiwa-bashi. Edges could be several hundred metres out.
properties.credit: Sketch by Project Tokyo from published descriptions (MLIT Tokyo Port Office; このまちアーカイブス)
properties.licence: Our own sketch; no third-party geometry.

properties.label: The Hibiya inlet, open sea at the castle's foot until filling began in 1592 (a sketch)
properties.source: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Realty. (n.d.). 「日比谷入江」の埋立て [Filling the Hibiya inlet]. このまちアーカイブス. https://smtrc.jp/town-archives/city/hibiya/index.html?id=a01 ; Kanto Regional Development Bureau, Tokyo Port Office. (n.d.). 東京港の変遷. https://www.pa.ktr.mlit.go.jp/tokyo/history/pdf/e-do01.pdf
properties.method: Drawn by hand: a shallow bay from Marunouchi south to Shimbashi, between the terrace foot and the Edo-maejima spit (Ginza). Shape is a guess from the descriptions.
properties.credit: Sketch by Project Tokyo from published descriptions (このまちアーカイブス; MLIT Tokyo Port Office)
properties.licence: Our own sketch; no third-party geometry.

properties.label: Early Edo about 1632, built-up land traced from the Kan'ei map
properties.source: 武州豊嶋郡江戸庄図 [Map of Edo, Toshima District, Musashi Province] (c. 1632; later reproduction). Tokyo Metropolitan Library, TOKYOアーカイブ, A13-003. https://archive.library.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/da/detail?tilcod=0000000013-00042417
properties.method: The drawn town was outlined on the scan and fitted to 11 landmarks, with a typical error of about 278 m. The map's frame cuts off the town's edges, and Sensō-ji, Shinagawa and Zōjō-ji lie outside it, so this ring understates the city.
properties.credit: Traced from 武州豊嶋郡江戸庄図, Tokyo Metropolitan Library (東京都立中央図書館), public domain
properties.licence: Source image public domain (Tokyo Metropolitan Library); tracing is our own.

properties.label: The shogunate's official city limit of 1818, the red line (shubiki)
properties.source: 旧江戸朱引内図 [Map of the red line of old Edo] (1818). Tokyo Metropolitan Archives, call no. 654-02-02-07 (ZA-113). https://dasasp03.i-repository.net/il/meta_pub/G0000002tokyoarchv01_0001001930001 ; Tokyo Metropolitan Archives. (n.d.). 江戸の範囲 [The extent of Edo]. https://www.soumu.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/01soumu/archives/0712edo_hanni.htm ; Geospatial Information Authority of Japan. (n.d.). 明治期の低湿地 [Lowlands of the Meiji era] map tiles (shoreline). https://maps.gsi.go.jp/development/ichiran.html
properties.method: The red line was traced from the archive's scan of the original 1818 map and pinned to 23 landmarks along it (bridges, river bends, villages on either side), keeping the drawn shape between them; edges may be several hundred metres out, most in the north-west and north-east. The map leaves the line open on the bay, so it was closed along the shore of the 1880s maps, which had barely moved since 1818.
properties.credit: Traced from 旧江戸朱引内図 (1818), 東京都公文書館 | Shoreline: 国土地理院「明治期の低湿地」
properties.licence: Traced from the public-domain 1818 map; our own polygon, CC BY 4.0. Shoreline from GSI map tiles (国土地理院コンテンツ利用規約, CC BY 4.0-compatible).

properties.label: Late Edo, mid-1800s: the townspeople's quarters only (samurai estates and temple land, most of the city, are left out)
properties.source: ROIS-DS Center for Open Data in the Humanities. (2024). 「江戸切絵図」町家領域データセット [Edo kiriezu townhouse-area dataset] (version of 2024-10-22). doi:10.20676/00000446. https://doi.org/10.20676/00000446
properties.method: Only the townspeople's land drawn on the Owariya-edition kiriezu maps (1849–62) is openly licensed, so the ring is that land merged, with gaps under 200 m (streets, canals) closed, holes under 1 km² filled and pieces under 0.05 km² dropped. Samurai estates, temples and shrines covered most of Edo and are not in it, so the ring shows where townspeople lived, not the whole built-up city.
properties.credit: 「江戸切絵図」町家領域データセット（ROIS-DS人文学オープンデータ共同利用センター作成）doi:10.20676/00000446
properties.licence: CODH dataset, CC BY 4.0; our merged polygon, CC BY 4.0.

properties.label: The city about 1909, built-up land traced from the survey map (sheets surveyed 1909)
properties.source: Tani, K. (2017). 今昔マップ旧版地形図タイル画像配信・閲覧サービスの開発 [Development of the Konjaku Map old topographic map tile service]. GIS: Theory and Applications, 25(1), 1–10. Map tiles: 今昔マップ on the web, Kanto/Tokyo 1:50,000 series 'tokyo50', https://ktgis.net/kjmapw/ Period '2man' (1:20,000, 1896–1909).
properties.method: A spot counts as built-up where ink covers over 70% of the 320 m square around it, over half of it dark. Strips under 220 m wide were removed, gaps under 10 km² filled, and only the main mass and pieces over 1.5 km² kept.
properties.credit: 「今昔マップ on the web」（(C)谷 謙二）より作成 — https://ktgis.net/kjmapw/
properties.licence: Our own polygons computed from the map images; the tiles were read once, then discarded, and are never re-served.
